question:
(i) Explain the difference between coherent and incoherent addition of light waves.
(ii) Two light waves have intensities $9I$ and $4I$. Calculate the resultant intensity when they are incoherent.
(iii) For the same two waves, calculate the maximum and minimum intensities if they are coherent.

options.A:
(i) Coherent waves have random phase difference, while incoherent waves have constant phase difference.
(ii) The incoherent resultant is $25I$.
(iii) The coherent maximum and minimum are $13I$ and $13I$.
options.B:
(i) Coherent waves have the same frequency and a constant phase difference, so their intensity depends on phase: $I=I_1+I_2+2\sqrt{I_1I_2}\cos\phi$. In incoherent addition, phase varies randomly, so the average interference term is zero and intensities add.
(ii) For $9I$ and $4I$, incoherent resultant is $13I$.
(iii) Coherent maximum is $(3\sqrt I+2\sqrt I)^2=25I$ and minimum is $(3\sqrt I-2\sqrt I)^2=I$.
options.C:
(i) Coherent and incoherent waves always add by ordinary intensity addition.
(ii) The resultant is $5I$.
(iii) The maximum is $13I$ and the minimum is $0$.
options.D:
(i) Incoherent waves interfere with fixed phase difference.
(ii) The incoherent intensity is $I$.
(iii) The coherent maximum and minimum are $9I$ and $4I$.
